ai.description: This frog reaches 25–30 mm. It is brown with a distinct cream-colored throat and granular skin. It is identified by its pointed snout and prominent, fleshy, triangular webbing on the toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus mewasinghi* is uniquely distinguished by its distinctively pointed, snout-like projection at the tip of its head, which is absent in other night frogs.
ai.habitat: *Nyctibatrachus mewasinghi* inhabits the evergreen forests of the southern Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 800 and 1,100 meters.
ai.behavior: Mewa Singh’s Night Frog is strictly nocturnal, remaining hidden in rock crevices or under leaf litter during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus mewasinghi* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 20–40 eggs on wet rocks or vegetation, which undergo direct development without a tadpole stage.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus mewasinghi* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically found at elevations between 200 and 1,100 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Nyctibatrachus mewasinghi* consists of a series of short, high-pitched "ticking" notes, typically heard along rocky streams in forest habitats.
